manifest.author: Codex operator, source-authored; not external expert certification
limits: Only four remediation capabilities in one historical training source group.
Training and development share source rules; their task constructions are distinct, not independent source domains.
Eight warehouse/business regression checks use training-partition sources; report separately from the twelve source-separated checks.
Known-source retention can include past P1 exposure; it is not an unseen-knowledge test.
No real Agent tool-use or process-execution capability is measured. That separate task is not a gate for freezing this knowledge-MCQ candidate packet.
No dataset release or training is implied until the downstream audit is complete.

amendments.before: A completed pick list has three separate instructions executed in order:
amendments.after: R and S name two distinct physical bin locations. A completed pick list has three separate instructions executed in order:
amendments.reason: The original symbols could denote SKUs rather than physical bins; unique locations must be stated explicitly.

amendments.before: Every completed instruction produced at least one event, and no event belongs to two instructions.
amendments.after: Every recorded event belongs to exactly one completed instruction; no events from unfinished instructions are included. Every completed instruction produced at least one recorded event.
amendments.reason: Completeness in the forward direction alone does not exclude events from unfinished instructions; distinct IDs must correspond exactly to completed instructions.
amendments.trigger: Operator premise audit and substantive reviewer objections, not closed-book score selection

amendments.before: J is the cheaper of the two allowed interventions.
amendments.after: Choosing J yields a lower total batching cost, including its fee, than choosing I.
amendments.reason: Cheaper intervention could mean its fee alone; the intended comparison is the complete resulting batching cost.
amendments.trigger: Operator premise audit and substantive reviewer objections, not closed-book score selection

amendments.before: Three feasible process designs start at 0.
amendments.after: Three proposed process designs start at 0; their compliance with the deadline and labor budget must be checked.
amendments.reason: Calling all designs feasible before checking the two constraints conflicts with the intended distinction between S, P and R.
amendments.trigger: Operator premise audit and substantive reviewer objections, not closed-book score selection
